config.advertiser_summary: Provider of affordable smart home security solutions, specifically video doorbells and security cameras starting at $60, targeting new homeowners, renters, and those concerned about package theft.

assumptions: Margin not given; assumed 55% (typical for home) for the break-even estimate only.
Break-even per customer (guidance, not enforced): $60 x 55% x 1.1 orders = $36.30.

pricing.rationale: Pay per click: verifiable without trusting a pixel. Maximise conversions within the budget: bids move between $0.25 and the $2.50 cap (category default) to spend it well; no CPA target is invented. Guidance: at the assumed margin, a click is worth about $0.44; bidding above that loses money per customer. Set a target CPA or a lower max CPC to enforce it.
pricing.tcpa_unlock: tCPA unlocks after conversion tracking is verified and 50 click-through conversions are recorded.

allocations.rationale: score 0.27, relative fit x1.40; 0.0096 conversions/$ at the start, falling as the host saturates; bid $1.75 (cap $2.50)
score 0.25, relative fit x1.36; 0.0096 conversions/$ at the start, falling as the host saturates; bid $1.70 (cap $2.43)
score 0.23, relative fit x1.28; 0.0096 conversions/$ at the start, falling as the host saturates; bid $1.60 (cap $2.28)

phases.name: learning
phases.rule: fixed start bid per host; pacing only
phases.why: stable bids so measured CTR/CVR aren't confounded

phases.name: maximize
phases.rule: bid = start x pacing x conversion likelihood, within [floor, cap]: spend the budget on the best opportunities
phases.why: no CPA target was set, so the goal is the most units for the budget

adjustments.reason: Under-delivering vs the daily plan -> bid up a little; over-delivering -> bid down.
Bid higher when the shopper looks like a likely converter (persona match vs the host's average shopper).

bid_strategy.rationale: Maximise conversions within the budget, never above the $2.50 cap (category default).
